_about: Honey CO2 estimate config. Model params come from EcoLogits' registry (hooks/eco-models.json), NOT hand estimates. This file only holds: grids, savings, and aliases for frontier models too new for the registry.
_engine: Faithful port of EcoLogits v0.8.2 (genai-impact/ecologits, MIT). scripts/eco_report.py runs the real package for the authoritative breakdown.
_match: A model id is resolved by: (1) exact name in eco-models.json, else (2) first alias whose 'match' substring appears in the id -> borrow that registry model's params, else (3) default_alias. Params and provider always come from the registry.
_grid_note: Per-provider, location-based. Anthropic on AWS Trainium (Project Rainier PA/IN/MS ~500), OpenAI on Azure (~400), Google on GCP (~330). Researched, not from EcoLogits; market-based (renewable PPAs) would be lower.
_savings_note: Output-token reduction vs a no-Honey baseline (CO2 scales with output tokens). This is a MODELLED counterfactual carried over from the benchmark — it is NOT measured for the session being reported, and every consumer must say so. 'full' is the paired per-task median from the committed stamp in savings_provenance (all task tiers, not the flattering code-only slice); lite/ultra keep their historical ratio to 'full' and remain extrapolations, never measured. Per tier on the same stamp: code -39% (p=0.007), user-facing -7% (ns, p=0.673), agent-to-agent -49% (n=2). $ savings run lower than CO2 since input isn't cut — and can go negative on a cold session.
_savings_provenance_note: Which measurement the ratio above came from. by_model gates the claim: a session whose model matches no key here gets NO savings line rather than an extrapolated one. An entry's 'n' overrides the suite-wide count when tasks were excluded (fable: cells with stop_reason 'refusal' — Fable 5 refuses some bare bench prompts — are dropped from pairing; see the stamp's report.md). Regenerate after a live bench with: node bench/src/report.js --stamp <stamp>

savings_provenance.method: paired per-task median delta in output tokens vs baseline; runs collapsed by median; two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank

_serving_note: EcoLogits' coefficient is a SINGLE-STREAM (batch-size-1) upper bound: it assigns one request the whole GPU set for the full generation latency (e.g. Opus ~1.9 tok/s, ~523s for 1000 tokens — ~30x slower than reality). Production serves many requests concurrently via continuous batching, which produces ~B tokens per forward pass at ~one-pass power, so per-request usage AND embodied impact (both latency-scaled) amortize by ~B. The badge and reports divide the faithful EcoLogits ceiling by this factor to show realistic SERVED impact; eco_report.py also prints the ceiling. 32 is calibrated so modeled throughput matches observed interactive serving (Opus 1.9 tok/s x 32 = ~61 tok/s, in the real ~50-70 tok/s range) and sits mid-range of published vLLM/TensorRT-LLM continuous-batching concurrency (16-64). Conservative by design — a carbon tool should not understate.
_aliases_note: For ids newer than the registry. Each points at the closest registry model whose EcoLogits params we borrow.
